sentences.nl: Hier oefenen we Nederlandse zinnen, met de grammatica van #dutchgrammar.
sentences.en: Here we practice Dutch sentences with the grammar of #dutchgrammar.

sentences.nl: Vandaag herhalen we de modale werkwoorden, uit les 28 en 29:, moeten, kunnen, mogen, willen en zullen.
sentences.en: Today we are reviewing the modal verbs from lessons 28 and 29: must, can, may, want, and will.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today repeat we the modal verbs, from lesson 28 and 29: must, can, may, want and will.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present tense "herhalen" (repeat) with the subject "we" (we) placed immediately after the verb, which is common in Dutch sentences.  
• The phrase "uit les 28 en 29" (from lesson 28 and 29) indicates the source or origin, using "uit" (from), a common preposition for this purpose.  
• The list of verbs, "moeten, kunnen, mogen, willen en zullen," are all modal verbs in Dutch, which are used similarly to English modals to express necessity, ability, permission, desire, and future actions.

• Extra phrases/examples:  
  - "Morgen gaan we de onregelmatige werkwoorden herhalen." (Tomorrow we will repeat the irregular verbs.)  
  - "Uit boek drie heb ik veel geleerd." (From book three, I learned a lot.)  
  - "We moeten de stof voor het examen herhalen." (We must repeat the material for the exam.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Vandaag bespreken we de nieuwe grammatica, uit hoofdstuk 5." (Today we discuss the new grammar, from chapter 5.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Modal verbs are a key part of language learning in Dutch, much like in English, and are often taught early in language courses to help express a range of basic needs and actions.

sentences.nl: En we praten over iets, wat heel belangrijk is voor Nederlanders:, de fiets!
sentences.en: And we are talking about something that is very important for the Dutch: the bicycle!

sentences.nl: De studenten brengen de koffers naar hun huisje.
sentences.en: The students take the suitcases to their cottage.

sentences.nl: Daar leren ze de andere studenten kennen.
sentences.en: There they get to know the other students.

sentences.nl: Iedereen zit lekker in het zonnetje.
sentences.en: Everyone is enjoying the sun.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Everyone sits nicely in the little sun.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• “Iedereen” means “everyone” and is a singular subject, so the verb “zit” is in the third person singular form.  
• “Lekker” in this context means “nicely” or “comfortably,” but it often means "tasty" when referring to food.  
• “In het zonnetje” literally means “in the little sun,” where “-tje” is a diminutive suffix. This phrase is idiomatic, suggesting enjoying the sun pleasantly.

• Example 1: Iedereen heeft het naar zijn zin. (Everyone is having a good time.)  
• Example 2: We zitten lekker op het terras. (We are sitting nicely on the terrace.)  
• Example 3: Het hondje ligt in het zonnetje te slapen. (The little dog is sleeping in the sun.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De kinderen spelen lekker in de tuin. (The children are playing nicely in the garden.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, enjoying the sun is a cherished activity, especially since the weather can be quite gloomy. Phrases like "zitten in het zonnetje" reflect the cultural value of enjoying sunny days when they occur.

sentences.nl: Op het bankje, maken ze plannen voor vanavond.
sentences.en: On the bench, they are making plans for tonight.

sentences.nl: Voor de barbecue.
sentences.en: For the barbecue.

sentences.nl: Anika en Jenn gaan een fiets huren.
sentences.en: Anika and Jenn are going to rent a bike.

sentences.nl: Dan kunnen ze naar de winkel.
sentences.en: Then they can go to the store.

sentences.nl: Ze lopen naar de fietsenverhuur.
sentences.en: They are walking to the bike rental.

sentences.nl: Wij willen een fiets huren.
sentences.en: We want to rent a bicycle.

sentences.nl: Dat kan.
sentences.en: That's possible.

sentences.nl: Je mag een fiets kiezen.
sentences.en: You may choose a bicycle.

sentences.nl: ‘Mag ik deze fiets?’, vraagt Jenn.
sentences.en: "May I have this bike?" asks Jenn.

sentences.nl: Dat mag.
sentences.en: That's allowed.

sentences.nl: Kan ik de fiets even proberen? — Ja hoor.
sentences.en: Can I try the bike for a moment? — Sure.

sentences.nl: Je kunt buiten een rondje fietsen.
sentences.en: You can ride a bike around outside.

sentences.nl: Eh…
sentences.en: Uh...

sentences.nl: Hoe moet dit? — Oh… hij staat nog op slot.
sentences.en: How does this work? — Oh… it's still locked.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• How must this? — Oh… it stands still on lock.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoe moet dit?" is a common way to ask "How should this be done?" or "How does this work?" The verb "moet" is the present tense of "moeten," meaning "must" or "have to."  
• "Hij staat nog op slot" means "It is still locked." The verb "staat" (stands) is used here to indicate a state or condition. "Op slot" means "locked."  
• Additional examples:
  - "Hoe werkt dit apparaat?" (How does this device work?)
  - "De deur staat open." (The door is open.)
  - "Hij moet naar huis." (He has to go home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hoe werkt deze machine? — Oh… hij is nog uitgeschakeld. (How does this machine work? — Oh… it is still turned off.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Op slot" is a common expression in Dutch to describe something that is locked, such as a door or a bike, reflecting the practical importance of security in everyday life in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Zal ik hem even van slot doen? — Ja graag.
sentences.en: Shall I unlock it for a moment? — Yes, please.

sentences.nl: De man pakt het sleuteltje.
sentences.en: The man picks up the little key.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The man grabs the little key.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De man" is the subject, meaning "the man."  
• "Pakt" is the verb in the present tense, meaning "grabs" or "takes."  
• "Het sleuteltje" is the direct object, meaning "the little key." The "-tje" ending is a diminutive form, often used in Dutch to indicate something is small or endearing.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Het kind eet een appeltje." (The child eats a little apple.)  
  - "Hij heeft een hondje." (He has a little dog.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De vrouw vindt het boekje. (The woman finds the little book.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch, diminutives like "-tje" are frequently used not just to indicate size but also to convey affection or familiarity.

sentences.nl: Jenn loopt met de fiets naar buiten.
sentences.en: Jenn walks outside with the bike.

sentences.nl: Ze controleert de fiets:, het stuur, het zadel, de wielen, de banden, de trappers
sentences.en: She checks the bicycle: the handlebar, the saddle, the wheels, the tires, the pedals.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• She checks the bike: the handlebars, the saddle, the wheels, the tires, the pedals.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "controleert" is the third person singular present tense of "controleren," meaning "to check" or "to inspect."  
• The sentence uses a list format after the colon, listing the parts of a bicycle.  
• "Het" and "de" are definite articles in Dutch, with "het" used for neuter nouns and "de" for common gender nouns. 

Extra phrases:  
• Hij controleert het huis: de ramen, de deuren, het dak. (He checks the house: the windows, the doors, the roof.)  
• Ze inspecteert de auto: de motor, de banden, de lichten. (She inspects the car: the engine, the tires, the lights.)  
• We controleren de documenten: de formulieren, de contracten, de facturen. (We check the documents: the forms, the contracts, the invoices.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze controleert de keuken: de oven, de koelkast, de kastjes. (She checks the kitchen: the oven, the refrigerator, the cabinets.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, cycling is a major mode of transportation. Regularly checking and maintaining a bicycle is common practice for safety and efficiency.

sentences.nl: ‘Eh… waar is de rem?’, vraagt ze aan de man.
sentences.en: "Uh... where is the brake?" she asks the man.

sentences.nl: Deze fiets heeft geen handrem,, maar een achteruittraprem.
sentences.en: This bicycle has no handbrake, but a backpedal brake.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This bike has no hand brake, but a back-pedal brake.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Deze fiets" means "this bike," where "deze" is a demonstrative pronoun for "de" words.  
• "Heeft geen" means "has no," where "geen" negates a noun.  
• "Achteruittraprem" is a compound word combining "achteruit" (backwards) and "traprem" (pedal brake). Compound words are common in Dutch.  
• Example 1: "Deze auto heeft geen airconditioning." (This car has no air conditioning.)  
• Example 2: "Hij heeft geen geld bij zich." (He has no money with him.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Deze stoel heeft geen armleuningen, maar is heel comfortabel." (This chair has no armrests, but is very comfortable.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, bicycles with back-pedal brakes are quite common, especially for city bikes. Many Dutch people grow up using them, and they are often preferred for their simplicity and reliability.

sentences.nl: Dit type rem vind je bijna alleen in Nederland.
sentences.en: You will find this type of brake almost only in the Netherlands.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This type brake find you almost only in Netherlands.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit type rem" means "this type of brake." "Type" is a noun modified by "dit" (this).  
• "Vind je" is an inverted word order, typical in Dutch for emphasis or questions. The verb "vinden" (to find) is in the present tense.  
• "Bijna alleen" means "almost only," where "bijna" is an adverb meaning "almost," and "alleen" means "only."  
• "In Nederland" is a prepositional phrase meaning "in the Netherlands." Prepositions like "in" are often used similarly to English.

Phrases:  
• "Dit soort weer zie je vaak in de zomer." (This kind of weather you often see in the summer.)  
• "Die oude auto vind je zelden buiten het museum." (That old car you rarely find outside the museum.)  
• "Dit type kaas komt alleen uit Frankrijk." (This type of cheese comes only from France.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dit soort muziek hoor je vooral op festivals." (This kind of music you hear mainly at festivals.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, there is a unique type of bicycle brake called a "coaster brake" that is quite common but not widely used elsewhere. This might be the type of brake referenced in the sentence.

sentences.nl: Om te remmen moet je achteruit trappen.
sentences.en: To brake, you have to pedal backwards.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• To brake must you backwards pedal.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses an infinitive clause "Om te remmen" (To brake) which is a common way to start sentences that describe a purpose or necessity.  
• "Moet je" (must you) indicates necessity or obligation, a common use of the modal verb "moeten."  
• "Achteruit trappen" (backwards pedal) describes the action needed to brake, commonly seen in bicycles with backpedal brakes.  
• Example: "Om te slagen moet je hard studeren." (To succeed, you must study hard.)  
• Example: "Om gezond te blijven moet je sporten." (To stay healthy, you must exercise.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Om te parkeren moet je langzaam rijden. (To park, you must drive slowly.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, bicycles with backpedal brakes (known as "terugtrapremmen") are common, especially for children. This sentence reflects typical advice given to someone learning to use such a bike.

sentences.nl: OK.
sentences.en: OK.

sentences.nl: Dat is belangrijke informatie!
sentences.en: That is important information!

sentences.nl: Eh… de banden staan een beetje zacht.
sentences.en: Eh… the tires are a bit soft.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Uh… the tires are a bit soft.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Eh…" is a filler word often used in Dutch to pause or think.  
• "De banden" is the subject, meaning "the tires." "Banden" is plural, with "de" as the definite article.  
• "Staan" is the verb, meaning "stand" or "are" in this context, indicating a state or condition.  
• "Een beetje" means "a bit" or "a little," used to lessen the adjective's intensity.  
• "Zacht" is an adjective meaning "soft," describing the state of the tires.

  - De koffie is een beetje koud. (The coffee is a bit cold.)  
  - De bloemen staan mooi in de vaas. (The flowers stand nicely in the vase.)  
  - Het water is een beetje warm. (The water is a bit warm.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De appels zijn een beetje zuur. (The apples are a bit sour.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, cycling is a common mode of transportation, and maintaining tire pressure is a routine part of bicycle maintenance. The phrase might often refer to checking bicycle tires.

sentences.nl: Hier is een fietspompje.
sentences.en: Here is a bicycle pump.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Here is a bicycle pump.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence follows a straightforward subject-verb-object order, with "Hier" indicating location or introduction.  
• "Hier" is often used to introduce or point out something in a nearby location.  
• "Een" is an indefinite article meaning "a" or "an."

Extra phrases:
- "Hier is een boek." (Here is a book.)
- "Hier zijn de sleutels." (Here are the keys.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hier is een kaart van de stad." (Here is a map of the city.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, cycling is extremely common, and having a small bicycle pump ("fietspompje") is quite practical and often necessary.

sentences.nl: Met dit fietspompje kun je de banden oppompen.
sentences.en: With this bicycle pump, you can inflate the tires.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• With this bike pump can you the tires up-pump.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "kun je," which is an inversion typical in Dutch questions and conditional statements, but here it's used in a statement to indicate possibility or ability.  
• "Oppompen" is a separable verb, where "op" is the particle that can separate from "pompen" (to pump). In the infinitive form, they stay together, but when conjugated, "op" can move to the end of the sentence.  
• Extra Examples:  
  - "Met deze sleutel kun je de deur openen." (With this key, you can open the door.)  
  - "Met die afstandsbediening kun je de tv aanzetten." (With that remote, you can turn on the TV.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Met deze pen kun je op glas schrijven. (With this pen, you can write on glass.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, biking is an essential part of daily life, and having a small bike pump (fietspompje) is common for quick repairs on the go.

sentences.nl: Moet ik dat doen? — ‘Ik zal het doen’, zegt de man.
sentences.en: Should I do that? — 'I will do it,' says the man.

sentences.nl: Zo… nu staan de banden weer hard.
sentences.en: So... now the tires are hard again.

sentences.nl: Nu kun je de fiets proberen.
sentences.en: Now you can try the bike.

sentences.nl: Jenn rijdt een rondje.
sentences.en: Jenn is driving a lap.

sentences.nl: ‘Hoe rijdt de fiets?’, vraagt Anika.
sentences.en: "How does the bike ride?" asks Anika.

sentences.nl: ‘Erg lekker…’, roept Jenn.
sentences.en: "Very tasty..." shouts Jenn.

sentences.nl: Ik wil deze fiets!
sentences.en: I want this bike!

sentences.nl: ‘Wil je veel fietstochten maken?’, vraagt de man.
sentences.en: "Do you want to go on many bike rides?" the man asks.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Want you many bike tours to make?" asks the man.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence is a direct question, with the verb "wil" (want) appearing first, followed by the subject "je" (you).  
• "Veel fietstochten maken" (to make many bike tours) uses "veel" (many) to modify "fietstochten" (bike tours), with "maken" (to make) as the infinitive verb.  
• "Vraagt de man" (asks the man) is a separate clause where "vraagt" (asks) is the verb, followed by the subject "de man" (the man).

Extra phrases:  
• "Wil je een kop koffie?" (Do you want a cup of coffee?)  
• "Vraagt de leraar of iedereen klaar is." (The teacher asks if everyone is ready.)  
• "We willen veel landen bezoeken." (We want to visit many countries.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wil je samen naar de film gaan?" (Do you want to go to the movies together?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Biking is a significant part of Dutch culture, with many dedicated paths and a strong emphasis on cycling as a mode of transportation and leisure. The Netherlands is known for its flat terrain, which makes it ideal for bike tours.

sentences.nl: Ja, vooral naar de discotheek!
sentences.en: Yes, especially to the nightclub!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Yes, especially to the disco!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ja" is a straightforward affirmative, meaning "yes."  
• "Vooral" is an adverb meaning "especially" or "mainly." It emphasizes the importance or preference for something.  
• "Naar" is a preposition meaning "to," used with directions or destinations.  
• "De discotheek" is a noun meaning "the disco" or "nightclub," where "de" is the definite article for common gender nouns in Dutch.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Vooral op zaterdag is het druk." (Especially on Saturday, it is busy.)  
  - "Ik ga naar de supermarkt." (I am going to the supermarket.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ja, vooral naar het strand!" (Yes, especially to the beach!)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, going to a "discotheek" is a popular weekend activity, especially among young people. They often have themed nights and play a mix of local and international music.

sentences.nl: De man moet lachen.
sentences.en: The man has to laugh.

sentences.nl: Je bent hier op het platteland.
sentences.en: You are here in the countryside.

sentences.nl: Hier zijn geen discotheken.
sentences.en: There are no nightclubs here.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Here are no discotheques.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence structure "Hier zijn geen..." uses a locative adverb ("hier") followed by a verb ("zijn") and a negation ("geen") to indicate absence.  
• "Geen" is used for negating nouns that are countable or indefinite, similar to "no" or "not any" in English.  
• Examples:  
  - Er zijn geen winkels in dit dorp. (There are no stores in this village.)  
  - Hier is geen water. (There is no water here.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hier zijn geen restaurants. (There are no restaurants here.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, discotheques are popular in urban areas but may be scarce in rural parts.

sentences.nl: Dan kun je beter, naar de Summer School in Amsterdam gaan.
sentences.en: Then you'd better go to the Summer School in Amsterdam.

sentences.nl: En trouwens, als je toch in het donker wilt fietsen…, doe dan altijd je licht aan!
sentences.en: And by the way, if you want to cycle in the dark anyway..., always turn on your light!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And by the way, if you indeed in the dark want to cycle..., do then always your light on!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En trouwens" (And by the way): This is a common phrase used to introduce an additional point or reminder.  
• "Als je toch" (if you indeed): "Toch" here implies a sense of insistence or emphasis, suggesting that the action will indeed happen despite potential objections.  
• "Doe dan altijd je licht aan" (do then always your light on): This uses the imperative form of "doen" (to do) and the separable verb "aandoen" (to turn on). In Dutch, separable verbs often place the prefix at the end of the clause.

Extra phrases:  
• "Als je toch gaat, neem dan een paraplu mee." (If you indeed go, then take an umbrella with you.)  
• "Doe je jas aan voordat je naar buiten gaat." (Put on your coat before you go outside.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En trouwens, als je toch naar de markt gaat, koop dan wat appels." (And by the way, if you do go to the market, then buy some apples.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, cycling is a major mode of transportation, and there are strict regulations about having lights on when cycling in the dark for safety reasons. It’s a common cultural practice to remind cyclists to use their lights at night.

sentences.nl: Hoe moet ik dat doen? — Dit is het voorlicht.
sentences.en: How should I do that? — This is the headlight.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• How should I that do? — This is the headlight.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoe moet ik dat doen?" uses an interrogative word order with "hoe" (how) leading the question. "Moet" is a modal verb indicating necessity or obligation, and it is positioned second.  
• "Dit is het voorlicht" is a simple declarative sentence where "dit" (this) is the subject, followed by "is" (is), and "het voorlicht" (the headlight) is the predicate.  
• Example extensions:  
  - "Hoe kan ik helpen?" (How can I help?)  
  - "Dit is mijn huis." (This is my house.)  
  - "Hoe werkt dit apparaat?" (How does this device work?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hoe kan ik dat repareren?" (How can I repair that?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, bicycles are a common mode of transport, and knowing how to fix or adjust parts like a "voorlicht" (headlight) is practical knowledge for many.

sentences.nl: En dit is de dynamo.
sentences.en: And this is the dynamo.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And this is the dynamo.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word "En" is a conjunction meaning "and," which is commonly used to link sentences or clauses.  
• "Dit" is a demonstrative pronoun meaning "this," used for singular, neuter nouns.  
• "Is" is the third person singular form of the verb "zijn" (to be).  
• "De dynamo" is a noun phrase. "De" is the definite article for common gender nouns, and "dynamo" means "dynamo."

• Extra Examples:  
  - "En dat is het probleem." (And that is the problem.)  
  - "Dit is mijn huis." (This is my house.)  
  - "Is dit jouw fiets?" (Is this your bike?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En dat is de oplossing. (And that is the solution.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, bicycles are a common mode of transportation, and many bikes use a dynamo to power lights. This sentence could easily occur in a conversation about bike maintenance.

sentences.nl: De dynamo zet je tegen het wiel.
sentences.en: You place the dynamo against the wheel.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The dynamo set you against the wheel.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Zet" is the verb "zetten" in present tense, second person singular, but here it implies an imperative form.  
• "Je" is used as the informal "you" or "your" here in imperative form, meaning "your" in this context.  
• "Tegen" is a preposition meaning "against."  
• "Het" is the definite article "the" used for neuter nouns.  
• "Wiel" means "wheel."  

Extra Sentences:  
• Zet het boek op de tafel. (Put the book on the table.)  
• Plaats de plant naast het raam. (Place the plant next to the window.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Plaats je fiets in de schuur. (Place your bike in the shed.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, dynamo-powered bicycle lights are common. The dynamo is a small generator that produces electricity to power the bike's lights as you pedal.

sentences.nl: ‘Hmm… het licht doet het niet’, zegt Anika.
sentences.en: ‘Hmm... the light isn't working,’ says Anika.

sentences.nl: Ja… je moet natuurlijk wel fietsen.
sentences.en: Yes… you do have to cycle, of course.

sentences.nl: Dan gaat de dynamo draaien en gaat het licht branden.
sentences.en: Then the dynamo starts turning and the light comes on.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Dan (Then)  
• gaat (goes/is going)  
• de dynamo (the dynamo)  
• draaien (to turn)  
• en (and)  
• gaat (goes/is going)  
• het licht (the light)  
• branden (to burn)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present tense with the verb "gaan" (to go), which can indicate a future or planned action in Dutch.  
• The structure "gaat [object] [verb]" is used twice here, showing sequential actions.  
• The conjunction "en" connects two clauses of equal importance.

Examples:  
• "Hij gaat de auto wassen en gaat daarna eten." (He is going to wash the car and then is going to eat.)  
• "We gaan naar de bioscoop en kijken een film." (We are going to the cinema and watch a movie.)  
• "Zij gaat de hond uitlaten en komt terug." (She is going to walk the dog and comes back.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij gaat de radio aanzetten en gaat dansen." (She is going to turn on the radio and is going to dance.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific cultural note applies to this sentence.

sentences.nl: Jenn rijdt nog een rondje.
sentences.en: Jenn is going for another round.

sentences.nl: Ja hoor, nu doet ie het!
sentences.en: Yes, sure, now it's working!

sentences.nl: ‘Voor mij ook zo’n fiets’, zegt Anika.
sentences.en: "For me too, such a bike," says Anika.

sentences.nl: Ze betalen de huur en een borg.

sentences.nl: Ken je de vervoeging, van de modale werkwoorden goed? — Dat is erg belangrijk.
sentences.en: Do you know the conjugation of the modal verbs well? — That is very important.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Know you the conjugation, of the modal verbs well? — That is very important.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ken je" is an inversion of "je kent," which is common in questions.  
• "De vervoeging" means "the conjugation," referring to verb forms.  
• "Modale werkwoorden" means "modal verbs," such as can, must, and may.  
• "Dat is erg belangrijk" uses "erg" to mean "very," and "belangrijk" means "important."

Extra Sentences:  
• Ken je de regels van het spel? (Do you know the rules of the game?)  
• Dat is erg duur. (That is very expensive.)  
• Begrijp je de betekenis van dit woord? (Do you understand the meaning of this word?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Begrijp je de vervoeging van sterke werkwoorden goed? (Do you understand the conjugation of strong verbs well?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Modal verbs in Dutch, like in English, are crucial for expressing necessity, ability, and permission. Understanding their conjugation is essential for clear communication.

sentences.nl: We gebruiken deze werkwoorden erg veel.
sentences.en: We use these verbs a lot.

sentences.nl: En ook de onderdelen van een fiets, moet je goed kennen.
sentences.en: And you also need to know the parts of a bicycle well.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And also the parts of a bike, must you well know.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses inversion due to the placement of "moet" after the comma, which is common in Dutch when the main clause follows an introductory element.  
• "Onderdelen" means "parts" or "components," which is a plural noun.  
• "Moet je goed kennen" translates to "must you well know," following the modal verb "moeten" (must). The verb "kennen" (to know) stays in its infinitive form because it follows the modal verb.  
• Similar structure: "De regels van het spel, moet je begrijpen." (The rules of the game, you must understand.)  
• Another example: "De ingrediënten van het recept, moet je verzamelen." (The ingredients of the recipe, you must gather.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En ook de basisprincipes van wiskunde, moet je goed begrijpen. (And also the basic principles of mathematics, you must understand well.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Cycling is an integral part of Dutch culture, and understanding bike maintenance is considered important. This sentence might reflect the practical mindset of ensuring safety and efficiency in cycling.
